Hypothetical, schematic: the centre pins the French armies against the fortress line — Rethel, Reims, Châlons, Troyes — while the wings close. Illustrates the concept.

Hypothetical, schematic: the 1st Army at full weight on the outer wheel — Amiens, Beauvais, west of Paris to the Seine at Mantes, south past Versailles and Étampes, then east through Fontainebleau and Sens to close the pocket near Troyes. Drawn at the march rates the historical army achieved; see the feasibility checklist for why that is the claim in dispute.

Hypothetical, schematic: the centre pins — Rethel, Reims, Châlons — and presses to the Seine at Troyes as the wings close.

Hypothetical, schematic: with no army forming at Paris and the German right behind its left, the 5th Army falls back south-east from Guise through Laon and Reims towards the Seine — and is caught between Troyes and the fortress line.
Hypothetical, schematic: the BEF retires south-west behind the Seine as Sir John French proposed on 31 August — Compiègne, Pontoise, Mantes, Chartres — out of the battle.

sources.note: Re-pointed from source:edmonds-1922 to the third edition, which is the one that is digitised and was read. p. 246 prints the proposal this hypothetical path begins from: "Sir John French proposed to retire 'westwards' behind the Seine, to an area just west of Paris ; but it was pointed out to him by the French General Staff that such a march would cross the communications of the Sixth Army." The day is 20 October — five days after this path begins, and worth knowing: before the 20th the French troops in Flanders were there but not yet this formation. p. 103 gives where they were on 15 October: the 87th and 89th Territorial Divisions under General Bidon "Between Poperinghe and Ypres", the French Naval Brigade at Dixmude.
